title: Bajaj Finance launches ₹11,700-crore QIP at ₹992.25 per share - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Bajaj Finance has launched a qualified institutional placement with a floor price of ₹992.25 per share to raise funds for expansion. | Photo Credit: iStockphoto

India's ​Bajaj Finance launched a more than $1 ‌billion share sale to institutional investors ​on Wednesday, setting ⁠the floor price at ₹992.25 apiece.

The non-bank lender in October approved ‌raising up to ₹11,700 crore ($1.25 billion) through a ‌qualified institutional placement.

The fundraise will ‌help ⁠Bajaj Finance, one of ⁠the country's biggest non-bank lenders, expand amid strong credit demand in India.

Bajaj Finance's assets ​under management ‌grew 26% year-on-year in the September quarter, the fastest pace since the March 2025 quarter.

A day ‌earlier, the company approved the ​issuance of warrants worth up to ₹5,800 crore to its holding company, Bajaj Finserv.

Bajaj Finance's capital adequacy ratio ‌stood at 20.33% as of September-end, down from 20.90% three months earlier and 21.23% a year ago.

The company's shares ended 1.3% higher on Wednesday. ‌They are up 9% so far in ​2026, supported by a recent rally in broader markets ⁠on easing crude oil prices and ⁠optimism over foreign inflows. The Nifty 50 index is ‌down around 3% this year.
